analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Markets are focused on three themes in the last week of October: France, Iran and AI. Brazil's surprise election result is also a watch item, with derivatives implying a -25% currency-adjusted decline in Brazilian equities.

France: protests over the weekend were smaller than the previous weekend. Moody's kept France at Aa3 (negative outlook) on Friday, against market expectations of a one-notch cut. French bond futures are up nearly three-quarters of a point and EUR is +0.13%.

Middle East: the pause in direct US-Iran fighting looks fragile. Media reports say Washington and Israel are considering renewed strikes after the US midterms, 8 days away. Trump said it is "getting to be decision time" on resuming attacks or making a deal. Disruption around the Strait of Hormuz is a key market risk.

Israel's election tomorrow (the sixth since 2019) is polling deadlocked, with neither bloc near the 61 seats needed. A result that weakens Netanyahu could lower the odds of Israeli-led escalation. A stalemate or a Netanyahu-led coalition leaves the incentive for renewed military action intact.
AI: Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday and Amazon Thursday. The market reaction, especially to capex plans, could rival Wednesday's FOMC and may matter more than the Fed, ECB or BoJ this week.

Fed (Wednesday): DB economists expect no change. Futures price under a 10% chance of a hike, after a brief spike above 50% under two weeks ago following the CPI print. The focus is Chair Warsh's press conference. DB expects a hawkish message and a statement with limited changes, though dissents to a hold are possible. Warsh is expected to say tighter financial conditions do not substitute for higher policy rates.

Thursday is the biggest US data day: September core PCE tracked at +0.36% MoM (3.14% YoY absent revisions, with August PPI revisions possibly keeping it from rounding up to 3.2%), and advance Q3 GDP expected at +3.3% annualised vs +2.2% in Q2. Friday's Q3 employment cost index is the labour-cost read.

Central banks: DB expects the ECB (Thursday) and BoJ (Friday) to hold, with under 3% market probability of a hike at either. Markets price 85% for a Bank of Canada hike and 88% for an RBNZ hike on Wednesday.

Eurozone flash October inflation is due Friday. DB expects headline CPI of 2.92% YoY in Germany, 3.58% in France and 4.95% in Italy. Preliminary Q3 GDP also prints for Germany, France, Italy and the Eurozone.

Brazil: Lula won a record fourth term 51.8% to 48.2% over Flávio Bolsonaro, after trailing 45.1%-47.0% in the first round. A Tokyo-listed Brazil equity ETF fell about -15% in Asian trading and derivatives imply a -10% move in the real. The rightward shift in Congress (right and centre-right Senate share 47% to 63%) should constrain a looser fiscal agenda. The open question is whether Lula can set a credible fiscal path.

Last week the Franco-German 10yr spread widened +29.5bps (−6.8bps Friday) to 167bps, near the Euro Crisis closing peak of 189bps. France's 10yr OAT yield rose +21.5bps to 5.01% and the 10yr Bund fell -8.0bps to 3.34%. CAC 40 fell -2.19% and STOXX Banks -5.10%, to their lowest since March and June respectively.

AI names stayed under pressure. The Philly semiconductor index fell for a third week (-3.21%), Nasdaq -0.71% and S&P 500 -0.47%. CoreWeave fell -11.65% with its 5yr CDS +19bps to 1146bps. Meta fell -9.40% after earnings, with its 5yr CDS +22bps to 127bps.

Energy: Brent rose for a third week (+6.24%) to $116.72/bbl, near the $118.35 post-2022 peak from March. European gas futures hit a post-2022 high of €93.85/MWh. A New York Times report said the US and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms.

Credit: spreads widened across US HY (+6bps), EUR HY (+40bps), US IG (+5bps) and EUR IG (+15bps). US HY widened for a 6th straight week, the first time since 2022. Pressure is concentrated in the weakest credits (US CCCs +59bps vs BBs +3bps and Bs +8bps), not indiscriminate HY selling.
Asia this morning: KOSPI -0.90% leads declines on tech weakness. Hang Seng +0.51% and ASX 200 +0.17% outperform. S&P 500 futures +0.20% and Nasdaq futures +0.24%.
Major earnings this week beyond US megacap tech include SK hynix (Wed), Samsung Electronics (Thu), Eli Lilly, Visa, Mastercard, Intel, Caterpillar, ExxonMobil, Chevron, Boeing and Shell.

France: weekend protests and fiscal concerns, with Moody's maintaining Aa3 (negative outlook).
Brazil: Lula wins the presidential runoff. Bolsonaro is challenging the result.
China's Central Committee plenum runs through Thursday. EU-Canada summit Oct 29-30. G20 foreign ministers meet in Atlanta Oct 30-31.

tension_points.bear_case: Another stalemate or a Netanyahu-led coalition could leave the incentive for renewed military action intact.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Israeli election result on Oct 27 showing neither bloc near the 61 seats needed, leading to protracted coalition talks or fresh elections.

tension_points.bull_case: The rightward shift in Congress (Senate share 47% to 63%) should constrain a materially looser fiscal agenda.
tension_points.bear_case: Lula has promised a fiscal adjustment without specifying delivery, and debt concerns are already keeping rates high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lula failing to establish a credible fiscal path once the election premium and Bolsonaro's challenge to the result are digested.
